questions.question: In an RNN, the transition weight matrix used to update the hidden state from step t=1 to step t=2 is identical to the one used from step t=9 to step t=10.
questions.explanation: True. RNNs share the same weight matrices (W_hh) across all time steps.

questions.question: What is a major limitation of using One-Hot Encoding for word representation in large vocabularies?
options: It results in high-dimensional, sparse vectors and fails to capture semantic relationships between words.
It creates dense vectors that cause immediate gradient explosion.
It forces all words to have the exact same learned floating-point values.
It automatically drops words that appear less than ten times.
questions.explanation: One-hot vectors are high-dimensional, sparse, and have no notion of similarity between words.

questions.question: What is the direct consequence of the vanishing gradient problem on a vanilla RNN's performance?
options: The model weights update too quickly, leading to divergent training behavior.
The network struggles to learn long-term dependencies and forgets information from earlier time steps.
The network automatically overfits on structural data borders.
The activation maps double in size at every recurrent layer.
questions.explanation: Vanishing gradients cause the network to forget information from earlier time steps, making it struggle with long-term dependencies.

questions.question: DNA sequencing is an example of sequential data because the specific ordering of base pairs determines genetic meaning.
questions.explanation: True. DNA data is sequential because the order of base pairs determines the genetic information.

questions.question: Which Keras API class represents the standard implementation of the LSTM architecture cell?
questions.explanation: layers.LSTM is the Keras class that implements the LSTM architecture cell.

questions.question: Speech Recognition involves converting continuous sequential audio signals into structured text sequences.
questions.explanation: True. Speech recognition processes sequential audio signals to produce structured text output.

questions.question: Which parameter weights are shared across all time steps in a vanilla Recurrent Neural Network?
options: Only the input-to-hidden layer transition weights (W_xh)
All key transition matrices (W_xh, W_hh, W_hy), meaning the exact same parameters are applied at every time step.
None; each time step has its own unique, independent set of weight matrices.
questions.explanation: RNNs share all key transition matrices (W_xh, W_hh, W_hy) across all time steps.

questions.question: Which technique is commonly used to mitigate the exploding gradient problem in recurrent networks by capping gradients at a maximum threshold?
questions.explanation: Gradient clipping rescales gradients if their norm exceeds a threshold, preventing exploding gradients.

questions.question: A standard LSTM cell contains exactly two gates: an input gate and a sorting gate.
questions.explanation: False. A standard LSTM cell contains three gates: forget gate, input gate, and output gate.

questions.question: If a vocabulary contains exactly 10,000 unique words, what is the length of the one-hot encoded vector representing an individual word?
questions.explanation: One-hot vector length equals the vocabulary size. With 10,000 unique words, each vector has length 10,000.

questions.question: Recurrent Neural Networks and LSTMs serve as standard foundational architectures for modern Natural Language Processing (NLP) applications like sentiment analysis and chatbots.
questions.explanation: True. RNNs and LSTMs are foundational architectures for many NLP applications including sentiment analysis and chatbots.

questions.question: Gradient clipping modifies the architecture of an RNN by converting all hidden states into convolutional pooling nodes.
questions.explanation: False. Gradient clipping is a training technique that scales gradients; it does not modify the network architecture.

questions.question: The exploding gradient problem occurs when repeated multiplications cause gradients to grow excessively large, destabilizing model training.
questions.explanation: True. Exploding gradients occur when repeated multiplications during backpropagation cause gradients to grow excessively large.

questions.question: Which of the following falls under the category of sequential time-series data suitable for RNN analysis?
options: Stock market prices, weather patterns, and sensor telemetry tracked over time
A collection of individual unlinked profile pictures
A table containing stationary house sizes and city zip codes
The discrete hyperparameter pairs for grid optimization
questions.explanation: Stock market prices, weather patterns, and sensor telemetry are sequential time-series data suitable for RNN analysis.

questions.question: What is the primary responsibility of the Forget Gate within an LSTM cell?
options: To decide what information from the previous cell state should be discarded or removed from memory.
To select which parts of the current cell state will be exposed as the final output.
To transform text tokens into dense embeddings automatically.
To force the learning rate parameter to reset to zero.
questions.explanation: The Forget Gate decides what information from the previous cell state should be discarded or removed from memory.

questions.question: To use layers.LSTM in Keras, you must always flatten your sequences into a single global 1D vector before passing them into the recurrent cell structure.
questions.explanation: False. LSTM layers in Keras accept 3D inputs (batch_size, timesteps, features) directly without flattening.

questions.question: Why are standard Feed-Forward Neural Networks (FFNNs) unsuited for handling sequential data like text or speech?
options: They have too many parallel processing streams.
They inherently share weights across temporal dimensions automatically.
They process inputs independently and lack a mechanism to retain past temporal context or memory.
They require the input vector to be 3D at all times.
questions.explanation: FFNNs process inputs independently without any mechanism to retain past temporal context or memory.
